title: DeepSeek made AI cheap. Now it is raising $8bn and buying robots
excerpt: DeepSeek has reopened an $8bn funding round at a $74bn valuation and taken a stake in robot maker Unitree, days after warning of a price rise.
content_html:
DeepSeek spent early 2025 proving that a good AI model did not have to cost a fortune. This week it has been busy proving it can spend one. In a handful of days, the Chinese lab reopened a multi-billion-dollar fundraising. It took a stake in the country’s best-known robot maker. And it told customers it would charge them more.

An $8bn round, reopened

DeepSeek has restarted its second funding round, seeking close to $8bn, Bloomberg reported. The raise values the Hangzhou startup at about 500 billion yuan, or $74bn. Monolith Management, an early backer of the Chinese AI champion Moonshot, is in talks to join.

The round is a restart, not a fresh start. DeepSeek paused the process last month after leaked remarks from founder Liang Wenfeng to investors caused friction. The valuation has climbed since its first external round earlier this summer. That round closed near 350 billion yuan and roughly doubled Liang’s net worth to about $36bn.

The company wants to raise about as much again. Discussions are ongoing, Bloomberg cautioned, and the size, timing, and investor list can still change.

What the money is for marks the real shift. DeepSeek plans to spend part of it building its own data centres, led by a large facility in Inner Mongolia. The lab that made its name on efficiency now needs its own compute. On the same day the round resurfaced, it also warned users of a significant price rise. DeepSeek is quietly rewriting its own cheap-AI story.

A robot bet in the same week

The second move points somewhere new. DeepSeek has invested 140.8 million yuan, about $20.8m, in Unitree Robotics’ Shanghai listing, Reuters reported from a stock-exchange filing. The stake buys 2.31% of the offering’s strategic placement, with a 36-month lock-up. It reads as a commitment, not a trade.

Alongside it sits a pact to jointly develop AI models for humanoid robots. The two Hangzhou firms will pair DeepSeek’s models with Unitree’s work in motion control and embodied intelligence. Each will favour the other, Unitree for training services, DeepSeek for robots. The target is the field’s hardest problem.

Can a robot “brain” make sense of an unfamiliar room and turn an instruction into a reliable action?

The pairing is telling. DeepSeek’s models are strong on coding, maths, and reasoning. But that strength sits in language, not in the multimodal systems that read the physical world. Its VL2 vision research was never folded into the flagship. A separate visual-reasoning project appeared and then vanished in April without explanation.

Unitree offers the missing half, robots and the scarce physical-world data they generate.

A rich price for the hardware

Unitree priced its IPO on Thursday, the payoff of a listing TNW has tracked since its earlier 50-billion-yuan target. It will raise about 6.1 billion yuan, or $904m, at a valuation near $9bn, Reuters reported. That makes it the first humanoid-robot maker to list on the mainland. Backers already include vehicles tied to Tencent, Alibaba, and China Mobile.

The numbers are steep. At 150.80 yuan a share the offering carries a price-to-earnings ratio of 219.

The industry average is near 39, according to Chinese outlet Cailian Press. Revenue more than quadrupled to 1.7 billion yuan in 2025, and humanoids became the biggest line. But first-quarter profit, stripped of one-offs, fell 52.6% as research and marketing costs climbed. US sales, 13.3% of last year’s revenue, sit exposed to fresh American curbs on Chinese robots.

Put the three moves together and a pattern shows. The company that proved AI could be cheap is now raising billions, building data centres, and charging more. It is also buying into machines that move.

DeepSeek is betting that the next phase will not be cheap at all. Whether the market that fell for the discount will pay the new price is the open question.

content_html_zh:
DeepSeek 在 2025 年初证明了一个好的人工智能模型并不需要花费很多钱。 本周，它一直忙于证明自己可以花一美元。 几天之内，中国实验室重新启动了数十亿美元的筹款活动。 它入股了该国最著名的机器人制造商。 它还告诉客户将向他们收取更高的费用。

80 亿美元融资重新启动

据彭博社报道，DeepSeek 已重启第二轮融资，寻求近 80 亿美元资金。 此次融资对这家杭州初创公司的估值约为 5000 亿元人民币（740 亿美元）。 Monolith Management 是中国人工智能冠军 Moonshot 的早期支持者，目前正在洽谈加入事宜。

本轮比赛是重新开始，而不是新的开始。 DeepSeek 上个月暂停了这一进程，原因是创始人梁文峰向投资者泄露的言论引起了摩擦。 自今年夏天早些时候进行第一轮外部融资以来，估值已经攀升。 该轮融资完成近 3500 亿元人民币，梁的净资产大约翻了一番，达到约 360 亿美元。

该公司希望再次筹集同样多的资金。 彭博社警告称，讨论仍在进行中，规模、时间安排和投资者名单仍可能发生变化。

钱的用途标志着真正的转变。 DeepSeek 计划花费一部分资金建设自己的数据中心，由内蒙古的一个大型设施牵头。 以效率闻名的实验室现在需要自己的计算。 在该轮融资重新出现的同一天，它还警告用户价格将大幅上涨。 DeepSeek 正在悄然改写自己的廉价人工智能故事。

机器人在同一周下注

第二个举措指向新的地方。 据路透社从一份证券交易所备案文件报道，DeepSeek 已在 Unitree Robotics 在上海上市的过程中投资了 1.408 亿元人民币（约合 2080 万美元）。 该股份购买了本次发行战略配售的 2.31%，锁定期为 36 个月。 它读起来是一种承诺，而不是一种交易。

除此之外，还有一项共同开发人形机器人人工智能模型的协议。 这两家杭州公司将把 DeepSeek 的模型与 Unitree 在运动控制和体现智能方面的工作结合起来。 双方都会偏爱对方，Unitree 提供培训服务，DeepSeek 提供机器人。 目标是该领域最难的问题。

机器人“大脑”能否理解陌生的房间并将指令转化为可靠的行动？

配对很能说明问题。 DeepSeek 的模型在编码、数学和推理方面都很强大。 但这种力量在于语言，而不在于读取物理世界的多模式系统。 它的 VL2 视觉研究从未并入旗舰产品中。 一个单独的视觉推理项目出现了，然后在四月份消失了，没有任何解释。

Unitree 提供了缺失的一半、机器人以及它们生成的稀缺物理世界数据。

硬件价格丰富

优树于周四为其 IPO 定价，TNW 上市后的回报自早先设定的 500 亿元人民币目标以来一直在跟踪。 据路透社报道，该公司将筹集约 61 亿元人民币（9.04 亿美元），估值接近 90 亿美元。 这使其成为第一家在大陆上市的人形机器人制造商。 支持者已经包括与腾讯、阿里巴巴和中国移动相关的机构。

数字非常陡峭。 此次发行价格为每股150.80元，市盈率为219倍。
